messages.author: bcfb6bc9f75aae0f
messages.subject: Can't install Rstan 2.3
parts:
Dear list,

Trying to follow the procedure written out at the RStan Getting Started page, I find myself (today July 4th, 2014) unable to proceed : in fact, the "http://mc-stan.org/rstan/install.R" address redirects back to the Stan Project Home page.

Ouch !

It is probably a glitch (I have already installed rstan on other machines using the same procedure) ; is that a (curious) way for the Stan gang to enforce US national holiday ?

Heads, up, someone ?

--
Emmanuel Charpentier

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can't install Rstan 2.3 [Cygwin/Rtools issues]
parts:
Yes, that's how it should look, with Rtools\bin before cyginwin64\bin.

That's been the problem before with users with Cygwin installed
on Windows.

There are instructions for compiling RStan under Cygwin in the
CmdStan manual (those need to move to the RStan doc):

https://github.com/stan-dev/cmdstan/releases/download/v2.3.0/cmdstan-guide-2.3.0.pdf


These are for 64-bit R and 64-bit Cygwin
==================================================================

• Kill all Cygwin bash shells and shut down R.

• After installing R and Rtools, make sure that R and Rtools are in the PATH environment variable. My R installation directory was c:\Program Files\R\R-3.0.1 and my Rtools installation directory was c:\Rtools, so I added the following to the end of my user PATH variable:

• C:\Program Files\R\R-3.0.1\bin\x64
• C:\Rtools\bin
• C:\Rtools\gcc-4.6.3\bin

• Now there could be a conflict between Cygwin and Rtools when running a bash shell under Cygwin, so I added the following lines to my .bash_profile file to remove any PATH directory referencing Rtools:

> TMP=`echo $PATH | /usr/bin/tr ':' '\n' \
| /usr/bin/egrep -iv '^/cygdrive/c/Rtools/' \

| tr '\n' ':'`

> PATH=${TMP%:}

(Note that the backslash characters signal that the line continues after a return.) This was only necessary to allow me to continue using Cygwin.

• Apparently there is something in Rcpp or inline or rstan that doesn’t like UNC paths. My home directory was \\server\users\kevinv and apparently this caused my local R library directory to be \server\users\kevinv\R as verified by .libPaths() from the R command prompt.

I fixed this by copying the entire directory tree rooted at \server\users\kevinv\R over to a local directory on my worksta- tion, C:\Users\KevinV\R, then adding the user environment variable R_LIBS_USER=C:\Users\KevinV\R. I shut down R and restarted it.

• At this point the instructions given for installing Rstan finally worked.

==========================end outtake===============================

- Bob

> system('where make')
c:\Rtools\bin\make.exe
